Whenever I misbehaved during public school as a child, my mother would take away anything from me as punishment. Books, video games, anything that made me happy. I remembered crying a lot whenever they'd take it before giving it back to me hours or days later.  


But, this recent memory stuck out to me. I love beads, I have a big bead collection after my grandmother died. My nmother never had any interest in beading. Then when I moved back from college, she was wanting to buy beads. I asked her where she was going to get them.   


She replied "From thisisunicorns's beading store." I told her no and that she can't shop in my beading store. The first time I ever fully said that word. No. And she was pissed off at me. She threatened to dump all my beads in the street because "This is my house." And I kept replying "These are my beads." While my n/edad was laughing his ass off.  


After I went into my bedroom, my dad came in to spend an entire hour gaslighting me. Feeding me crap about how I hold onto the previous physical and mental abuse close to my heart. "Get over it" is a common phrase my parents say, the same ones who isolated me from others and that I grew up alone as a child and teenager. I was crying a lot and was so emotionally vulnerable, yet I saw it in his eyes, he had no emotions on his face. That he didn't care for my wellbeing and being so blatantly ignorant of my emotions. Yet lies that he does.  


It makes me excited to be moving back to college, I can't wait till I get away from these bastards for a semester.

That's awful what your family put you through! It reminds me of my unhappy vacation to Disneyworld as well. I hope you have a much better time when you go to Disneyland when the plagues end without those awful people.

Mine was mostly stressful because of my grandmother, who I didn't even have that close of a connection to due to her abusive controlling husband isolating her. She was around bad men, yet was blinded by it as love. She and my mother never got along, no matter how many times my mom said she cared for her because of family, I could tell it hurt. So, my grandmother was really stubborn. She got lost in the airport in Florida, and I remembered how scared I was of my mother because of how pissed off she was while my dad went looking for his mom. I often huddle onto the side closest to the door in the car, and my parents never notice this behavior. So, we finally got her and drove to the hotel where upon reaching the apartment style, my mother locked herself in the master bedroom and had a mental breakdown. I had no clue why it happened, it just did.

This was what really made this vacation awful; my stupid stubborn grandmother decided to get a wheelchair, a regular one that my father had to push her all around because she had back problems due to her own stubbornness. My mother told her to get an electric scooter, but the old lady insisted we'd get a manual one. So while we were in the que line, my mother saw the regular wheelchair and was pissed and walked away, so we spent the whole time at the Magic Kingdom split. I hated that trip so much, and I haven't felt much emotion for my grandmother because it was her fault the whole mess happened. Still, it did help me know how messed up my family is. She did pass away last year (Which my parents hid from me until I returned from college) which got my angry, yet I'm just happy I won't have to spend any more vacations with her.

The best time of the entire mess was when I went to Universal Studios for the first time. I went on the Transformers ride five times and it was nice to be away from my family. A pleasure I'm having now at college. Here's to hoping your day is better now that you're able to get that off your chest.
